standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverse
standard_prerequisites.statement: A quasi-inverse for f is a triple of a map g and homotopies from the composites to the identity maps.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the assumed datum (g, eta, epsilon) at source line 219.

standard_prerequisites.name: Half adjoint equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: A half adjoint equivalence is a quadruple of a map, its inverse and two homotopies together with a coherence path between the two ways of composing them.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quadruple (g-prime, eta-prime, epsilon-prime, tau) that the proof has to produce at source line 220.

standard_prerequisites.name: Naturality of the two homotopies
standard_prerequisites.statement: The homotopies of a quasi-inverse satisfy naturality squares relating them to the maps on paths.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two labelled naturality results invoked at source lines 232-235 are what make the coherence path computable.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cancellation in identity types
standard_prerequisites.statement: From a common right factor in an identity type one may cancel to obtain an equality of the two left factors.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the last step that turns the computed identity into the required coherence path at source line 241.

core_obligations: Given a quasi-inverse (g, eta, epsilon) for f, keep g-prime equal to g and eta-prime equal to eta, and recognise that epsilon cannot simply be reused because the coherence datum has to be constructed (source lines 219-224).

Replace epsilon by the corrected family epsilon-prime(b) defined as the inverse of epsilon at f(g(b)) composed with the composite of the action of f on eta at g(b) with epsilon(b) (source lines 225-227).
State the coherence obligation tau(a), namely that the action of f on eta at a equals epsilon-prime at f(a) (source lines 228-231).

Rewrite eta at g(f(a)) as the action of g on the action of f on eta at a, using the naturality of eta, and then compute how the action of f on that composite interacts with epsilon(f(a)) by the naturality of epsilon (source lines 232-240).
Cancel the common right factor to obtain the required path tau(a) and thereby the half adjoint equivalence (source line 241).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix the obvious choices of the inverse and of the first homotopy, and see that the second homotopy needs correction.
Define the corrected homotopy and write down the coherence obligation.
Evaluate the two sides of the obligation with the two naturality results.
Cancel and read off the coherence path.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem thm:equiv-iso-adj at source lines 215-217: every quasi-inverse of a map f can be promoted to a half adjoint equivalence. The author's proof (source lines 218-242) cannot follow the most obvious route, because the second homotopy of the given quasi-inverse has to be replaced by the corrected family epsilon-prime(b) built from the inverse of epsilon at f(g(b)) and the action of f on eta at g(b) (source lines 222-227), and only then can the coherence path tau(a) be stated (source lines 228-231). Producing that path needs two separate computations: the naturality of eta rewrites eta at g(f(a)) as the action of g on the action of f on eta at a (source lines 232-234), and the naturality of epsilon moves the action of f on that composite past epsilon(f(a)) (source lines 235-240), after which the common right factor is cancelled (source line 241). The statement indicates neither that the second homotopy must be modified nor which naturality squares close the coherence.
